summary.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see’ and is the simplified form of 視. The older graph 視 is traditionally analyzed as 見, associated with seeing, plus 示 as a sound element. A separate early graph is interpreted as an eye above a standing figure.

formation.text: The visible 视 is the simplified counterpart of 視. In the received traditional graph, 見 contributes the seeing-related meaning and 示 supplies a phonetic cue. A proposed early graph is instead a whole pictorial form of an eye above a standing person; the two analyses describe different forms, not a demonstrated sequence of component changes.

components.text: Within the received graph 視, 見 is the semantic element associated with seeing. This role describes the traditional compound analysis; it does not establish that the earliest graph had this component structure.
Within 視, 示 is analyzed as the phonetic element. Its modern Mandarin reading matches 視, but that current match alone cannot prove the historical sound relationship.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin pair is attested, and a same-system historical comparison is reported, but the reconstruction table could not be inspected here; modern readings alone do not establish the ancient phonetic role.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 示 shì and 視 shì have matching readings. This comparison records their current sounds and does not by itself establish the historical role.

components.text: A proposed early form of 視 is interpreted as a whole picture of an eye above a standing figure. The drawing is a modern redraw of an oracle-style graph, not an artifact image; the interpretation remains scholarly and individual archaic forms may be disputed.

history.text: A paleographic interpretation distinguishes Shang oracle-bone forms read as 視 and 見 by the figure beneath the eye: standing in the form read as 視, seated in 見. The same analysis identifies standing-figure forms in Western Zhou bronzes and reports an early phonetic spelling using 見 and 氏 alongside the pictographic form. The curated oracle-style illustration is a modern redraw, and an earlier reading of the standing-figure form as 望 is reported and rejected.
The received traditional graph 視 is analyzed as 見 plus 示, with 見 semantic and 示 phonetic. The present character 视 is identified as the simplified form of 視.

uncertainties.text: The standing-figure reading is a scholarly interpretation, and individual archaic examples may remain disputed; no absolute date is supplied for a specific oracle-bone token. The supplied character accounts identify 视 as simplified from 視, though a character-specific official standard record was not retrieved.

示 is explicitly analyzed as phonetic in the traditional graph. A same-system reconstruction comparison with 視 was reported, but the table could not be inspected; current matching Mandarin readings do not establish the ancient sound relationship.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone evidence; individual token date unresolved
senses.text: The cited paleographic analysis identifies Shang oracle-bone contexts, including 視師 and 視方, as uses involving observing. The date of any individual token is not specified.

The received traditional graph is glossed as looking toward, and dictionary examples include examining or observing. When this use developed in relation to the basic looking or seeing sense is unresolved.
Current definitions include looking at, observing and seeing.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but their chronological or derivational relationship is not established.

limitations.text: Other dictionary-attested uses include treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating, and a use glossed as 通「示」. Their chronology and connections are not established here.

overview.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see’ and is the simplified form of 視. The early graph is interpreted as an eye above a standing figure; the received traditional graph is analyzed differently, with 見 for seeing and 示 for sound.

components.text: 見 links the traditional graph to seeing.
示 is analyzed as the sound element in the traditional graph.
The proposed early graph is read as one picture: an eye above a standing person.

relationships.text: The supplied character accounts identify 视 as the simplified form of 視.
In the received traditional graph 視, 見 is the semantic element associated with seeing.

The received traditional analysis assigns 示 the phonetic role in 視. Modern Mandarin 示 shì and 視 shì match, but that current pair does not establish the historical relation; the reported same-system reconstruction comparison was not independently inspected.
